matrix.api: ds.configure(ccxmlFile: string): CoreList{cores[],nonDebugCores[]}; ds.listCores(): CoreList; ds.deconfigure(): void
matrix.notes: configure does NOT connect cores; throws if already configured (deconfigure first; deconfigure disconnects all cores and invalidates sessions). Core name strings are probe+core (example uses XDS110 name); exact Blackhawk 560v2 core-name strings UNKNOWN until real ccxml.

matrix.api: ds.openSession(corePattern: RegExp|string = ''): DebugSession; session.getName(): string; session.getPartNum(): string; session.close(): void
matrix.notes: First matching core wins (regex). session.close() is NOT disconnect; target stays connected.

matrix.api: session.target.connect(): void; disconnect(): void; isConnected(): boolean
matrix.side_effects: connect runs OnPreTargetConnect/OnTargetConnect GEL (synchronous) from startup GEL in ccxml; GEL that modifies state (e.g. GEL_Reset) halts target and defeats unobtrusive connect. Unobtrusive connect only described for real-time mode.

matrix.api: session.settings.getDetailedSettings(): DebugSetting[]; get(id): boolean|number|string; set(id, value): void
matrix.notes: Documented IDs: AutoRunToLabelOnReset, AutoRunToLabelName, AutoRunToLabelOnRestart. Realtime mode / polite / 'Halt the target before any debugger access' setting IDs NOT given in docs -> discover via getDetailedSettings on real host (SDK check).

matrix.capability: attach second scripting instance to same debugger
matrix.api: initScripting({attach: handle|'auto'}); ds.getInstanceHandle(): number
matrix.notes: Docs say both instances can interact simultaneously. Whether a 2nd instance can issue halt/isHalted while the 1st is blocked in a call is NOT documented -> SDK check before using as control plane.

matrix.api: target.run(waitForHalt?: boolean = true): void; halt(): void; waitForHalt(): void; isHalted(): boolean
matrix.notes: run() blocks until halt by default -> bridge must call run(false). No run-state event/subscription API; state via isHalted() polling or GEL OnHalt callback (registerCallback).

matrix.api: target.stepInto(explicitlyAsm?: boolean=false); stepOver(explicitlyAsm?); stepOut()
matrix.notes: Blocks until halted again. Source step if symbols cover current PC, else asm step; explicitlyAsm forces asm.

matrix.api: target.getResets(): Record<string,boolean>; reset(resetType?: string): void; restart(): void
matrix.notes: Reset names are target-specific (query getResets). restart sets PC to entry, calls OnRestart GEL, may auto-run to label (setting). Prior survey: reset failure not thrown -> re-check state.

matrix.capability: multicore simultaneous run/halt/asm step; global breakpoint (cross-trigger)
matrix.api: ds.simultaneous.run(targets: string[], waitForHalt?=true); halt(targets); asmStepInto(targets); session.globalBreakpoint.enable()/disable()
registers.getRegisterGroups(groupId?: string|null): {registers: RegisterInfo[], groups: GroupInfo[]}; getBitfields(registerId): RegisterBitfield[]
matrix.notes: RegisterInfo{id,name,location?(undefined for core regs),readable,writable}; readable/writable still require target state allowing access. Bitfield type field is 'stop' in Types page but example destructures 'end' (doc inconsistency). Register/group names are target-specific: enumerate at runtime, do not hardcode.

matrix.api: registers.read(registerName: string): bigint|number|string; write(registerName, value: bigint|number|string): void; exportAsJson(groupIds, filePath, style?); importFromJson(filePath)
matrix.notes: 'PC' and 'R0' used in examples (Arm-like). SP/PC names for C28x/C6000/Cortex-R NOT verified by this reference -> discover from getRegisterGroups. Memory-mapped registers (RegisterInfo.location set) are MMIO: read may have side effects (read-to-clear) -> separate capability class.

matrix.api: memory.read(location: DSLocation, count: number, bitSize?: number): (bigint|number|string)[]; readOne(location, bitSize?)
matrix.notes: count = number of VALUES (not bytes). bitSize default = target word size; valid 8,16,24,32,40,48,64. Values returned as UNSIGNED integers. Endianness of returned values not stated (inference: debugger returns target-endian-interpreted integers) -> verify on HW. Page via 'addr@PAGE', '@pa', '@ipa'; memory.getPages(). Running-target access behaviour NOT stated in API -> device/mode dependent (A20).

matrix.api: memory.write(location, values[], bitSize?); fill(location, count, value, bitSize?); saveData/loadData/saveBinary/loadBinary; getSupportedFormats(page?)
matrix.notes: write truncates to bitSize, negatives written as signed. Action class (mutating).

matrix.api: memory.memMap.get(): {entries:[{start,end,attributes[]}], enabled}; add(start,length,readable,writable); enable(bool); remove(loc); reset()
matrix.notes: Map reflects GEL_MapAddStr attributes; useful to pre-validate ranges before read. It is debugger permission map, not a side-effect (read-sensitive) classification.

matrix.api: Address = bigint|string|number; DSLocation = Address | 'num@page'
matrix.notes: JS returns BigInt for integers; TI recommends BigInt/strings (JS number exact only to 53 bits). Python uses int. Bridge must serialize as hex/decimal strings in JSON (BigInt is not JSON-serializable).

matrix.api: n/a (target fact)
matrix.notes: C28x is 16-bit addressable: each address = 16 bits; char/byte = 16 bits; sizeof(int)==1. So 32-bit var = 2 address units; next element address += bitSize/16. memory.read(...,bitSize=8) behaviour on C28x NOT documented -> avoid/SDK check. Other TI cores (Cortex-R/M/A, C6000, C29x): address unit NOT verified in this pass -> per-target capability 'address_unit_bits' from config + HW acceptance.

matrix.api: session.symbols.load(fullPath): void (replace); add(fullPath); loadWithOffset/addWithOffset(path, codeOffset, dataOffset, relative?); remove(path); unloadAllSymbols()
matrix.notes: Explicitly 'loads only the symbol information' -> correct for already-flashed targets. Contrast memory.loadProgram (writes target + symbols; ELF/COFF/hex). Accepted file types for symbols.load not enumerated (examples use .out).

matrix.api: session.symbols.getAddress(symbol): bigint|number|string|null; lookupSymbols(start: DSLocation, length?=0): string[]

matrix.capability: enumerate all symbols / all source files
matrix.api: NOT FOUND
matrix.notes: No list-all-symbols or list-source-files API. Workaround (proposal): lookupSymbols over known memory ranges, or parse ELF on the Loom side (not a CCS API).

matrix.api: SymbolModule: symModule.lookupSourceLine(addr): {file,line}|null; lookupFunction(addr): {name,file}|null; via ds.openSymbolModule(processorId, isBigEndian=false); symModule.load/add/remove/unloadAll/close
matrix.notes: Works without target/session. processorId is an undocumented 'magic number' identifying the architecture -> values UNKNOWN, SDK check. Session-level Symbols has no lookupSourceLine.

matrix.api: session.callstack.fetch(maxLevels?): {frames:[{functionName?, sourceLine?{path,line,column}, pc: string, locals: string[]}], reasonUnwindHalted}
matrix.notes: Best documented path for 'PC -> file:line' in a live session. pc is string. path is presumably compile-time path (inference) -> needs path mapping.

matrix.api: NOT FOUND (no direct API)
matrix.notes: breakpoints.add(file,line) accepts file:line, and getProperty(id,'Hardware Configuration.Location') shows source-based location string, but getProperty is documented on PROPERTY-SET ids, not breakpoint ids -> do not rely. Proposal: Loom-side DWARF line table parse, or SDK check.

matrix.api: NOT FOUND in scripting API
matrix.notes: IDE has Source Lookup dialog / launch config (GUI). Breakpoint file arg = full compile-time path OR basename (first match). Mapping must be a Loom/bridge table (proposal).

matrix.api: symModule.disassemble(start: Address, end: Address): {disassembly:[{address, numOpCodes, text}]}
matrix.notes: Uses CONTENTS OF LOADED OBJECT FILES, inclusive range; text contains address+opcodes+instruction. Not live target memory -> mismatch if flash differs. Session-level live-memory disassembly API NOT FOUND. Needs processorId (unknown).

matrix.api: breakpoints.add(locationExprOrSrcFile: Address|string, line?: number): number; remove(id); removeAll()
matrix.notes: Location = address, symbol expression ('main + 0x8') or source file (+line).

matrix.capability: HW bp / condition / skip count / action
matrix.api: createProperties(type?: 0 sw|1 hw): number; setProperty(propsId, propertyId, value); setPropertySourceLocation(propsId, propertyId, file, line); getProperty(propsId, propertyId); getDetailedProperties(propsId): BreakpointProperty[]; addWithProperties(propsId): number
matrix.notes: Documented property ids: 'Hardware Configuration.Location', 'Debugger Response.Skip Count', 'Debugger Response.Action.Expression'. Condition exists under Debugger Response in debug guide (GEL expr) but exact id not given -> discover via getDetailedProperties. Properties only settable before add. Names vary per target/bp type.

matrix.capability: enable/disable without remove, list, hit state/count
matrix.api: NOT FOUND
matrix.notes: Bridge must own BP table (id->spec). Disable = remove + re-add (new id). Hit detection: after halt compare PC (registers.read / callstack) with BP address (derived, not an API), or GEL OnHalt via registerCallback (throws if device GEL already defines OnHalt).

matrix.api: expressions.evaluate(expression: string): void|bigint|number|string
matrix.side_effects: Evaluates GEL; can call built-in/user GEL functions and registered JS callbacks -> NOT inherently read-only. Integral->BigInt, float->number, other (e.g. C++ object ref) -> no value.
matrix.notes: Use symbols.getAddress + memory.read with known type for read-only watch; restrict evaluate to an allowlisted grammar or treat as action.

matrix.api: session.registerCallback(name, (ds, session, ...args) => boolean|float|bigint|string); registerMenuCallback(name, menu, cb)
matrix.notes: Debugger invokes OnHalt etc. if defined; throws if same-name GEL function exists (many device GELs predefine).

matrix.api: initScripting({timeout}); ds.setScriptingTimeout(ms) (<=0 disables); ds.getScriptingTimeout(); ScriptingTimeoutError
matrix.notes: Global for ALL future calls (not per-call). Default: no timeout. Docs do not state whether the underlying operation stops or target state after timeout (example then calls halt — Loom must NOT auto-halt). No cancel API: only timeout or process kill.

matrix.api: Synchronous API (since CCS Theia 1.3); sleep(ms) blocks event loop
matrix.notes: JS calls block the Node event loop -> a readline/JSON-lines loop in the SAME process cannot service STOP/heartbeat during a call. Need separate control process or explicit in-flight/uncancellable semantics.

matrix.api: memory.loadProgram(filepath, args?: string[]); loadBinaryProgram(filepath, startAddress); verifyProgram(filepath) (throws on mismatch); verifyBinaryProgram(filepath, startAddress)
matrix.notes: ELF, COFF, hex formats. Writes target. Excluded from MVP.

matrix.api: <CCS>/ccs/scripting/run.sh|run.bat <script>; JS outside: require(ccsPath + '/ccs/scripting/node_modules/scripting'); Python: <CCS>/ccs/scripting/python/run.sh or own Python>=3.10 with pip install -e <CCS>/ccs/scripting/python/site-packages/scripting; initScripting({ccsRoot}) if package relocated
matrix.notes: CCS bundles Node and Python 3.14. Every path points INTO a CCS install; external import still needs CCS install (+ device support + Blackhawk drivers per prior survey). Standalone minimal bundle NOT documented/verified. interactive.mjs = no IDE dependency (headless). launchCCS() optional side-by-side IDE (not needed).
